samples.summary: `index`/`count` bounded only by the axis length (1e6 for rows) lets one request build a million-entry axis array inside `doc.update` — event-loop stall/OOM, a `splice` spread RangeError, and eventual infinite loop when the 36^4 axis-ID space is exhausted
samples.evidence: `parseCount` (worksheet-structure.ts:143-156) and `parseIndex` (:123) accept any integer in 1..MaxRows (1e6). A body `{axis:'row', index:1, count:1000000}` reaches `insertWorksheetAxis` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-axis.ts:25-45), which mints `count` IDs via `createWorksheetAxisId` (one `crypto.getRandomValues` + Set lookup each) and then does `order.splice(index-1, 0, ...created)` — spreading ~1e6 arguments exceeds the engine argument limit and throws RangeError. Even `{index:1000000, count:1}` forces `ensureAxisLength` to push 999,999 CRDT array nodes synchronously inside `doc.update`, blocking the whole Node process and ballooning memory. Worst case: the ID alphabet is 36^4 ≈ 1,679,616 (worksheet-record.ts:77-103, `for(;;)` retry until unique); once an axis exceeds that many IDs — reachable with a handful of large inserts, all permitted by this validator — `createWorksheetAxisId` can never return and the server hangs permanently. The `clear` endpoint's own comment (:14-30) explains exactly this class of risk and caps the work; the new axis validator does not cap the work, only the coordinate.

samples.summary: The move endpoint skips the merge-split guard the editor applies, so an API move that partially overlaps a merged block silently drops the merge
samples.evidence: `Sheet.moveCells` refuses the whole operation when the source range partially intersects a merge: `for (const [anchorSref, span] of this.merges) { if (isMergeSplitByMove(anchor, span, axis, src, count)) return; }` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1466-1471). `moveAxis` calls `applyWorksheetMove` directly with no such check, and `moveMergeMap` drops any merge `moveMerge` cannot remap (`if (!moved) continue;`, packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/merging.ts:172). A `POST .../move` that half-crosses a merged block therefore moves the cells and deletes the merge span — state the UI is explicitly written to prevent.

samples.summary: Insert/delete/move leave `ws.filter`, `ws.hiddenRows`/`hiddenColumns` and `frozenRows`/`frozenCols` un-shifted, so index-keyed worksheet state points at the wrong rows/columns after an API structural edit
samples.evidence: `applyWorksheetShift`/`applyWorksheetMove` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts:273-418) touch cells, dimensions, styles, merges, CF/DV, anchors and chart ranges but never `filter`, `hiddenRows`, `hiddenColumns`, `frozenRows` or `frozenCols` (grep for `hiddenRows|filter` in that file returns nothing). The editor does those separately around the same engine call: `this.shiftFilterState(...)`, `this.shiftUserHiddenState(...)` (sheet.ts:1317-1318) and the freeze-pane expand/shrink block (sheet.ts:1334-1359). Those fields are persisted in the Yorkie doc and independently writable via `worksheet.controller.ts` (`PUT freeze`, `PUT hidden`) and `worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts` (`PUT filter`), so after `POST insert` the stored filter range, hidden-row indices and freeze boundary silently refer to shifted rows.
searchedFor: listed backend v1 controllers writing freeze/hidden/filter

samples.summary: Formula strings are rewritten but cached `v` values are never recalculated, so the document (and `GET /cells`) serves stale values after an insert/delete/move
samples.evidence: `rewriteFormulaCells` only rewrites `cell.f` (worksheet-structure.ts:80-96); the cached `cell.v` is carried over unchanged. The editor recalculates right after the same call (`await this.recalculateAllFormulaCells();`, packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1361, plus `recomputeFilterHiddenRows`). Deleting a row that a formula referenced leaves the dependent's `v` at its pre-delete value, and `ApiV1CellsController.getCells` returns `cell?.v` verbatim (cells.controller.ts:63-72), so API readers see values inconsistent with the formulas until some client opens the doc and recalculates. Grep for `recalc|calculate` under packages/backend/src returns nothing, so no backend path repairs this.

samples.summary: No guard against structural edits on a pivot-output or non-sheet tab; the editor refuses these outright
samples.evidence: `Sheet.insertRows/deleteRows/insertColumns/deleteColumns` all start with `if (this.pivotDefinition) return;` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1236,1244,1252,1260) because the tab's grid is generated output. `assertSheetDocument` only checks the *document* type ('sheet'), never the tab: `worksheetOrThrow` accepts any `root.sheets[tabId]`, including a tab whose `TabMeta.type` is 'datasource'/'lakehouse' or whose worksheet carries `pivotTable`. Rows inserted into such a tab are silently clobbered on the next materialization or desynchronize the generated grid.
searchedFor: read assertSheetDocument/worksheetOrThrow in the new controller

samples.summary: `index + count` is not bounded by the grid, so an insert can push rows/columns past the addressable grid (col > 18278 / row > 1e6) where the cells become unreachable
samples.evidence: `parseAxisShift` validates `index` and `count` independently against the same per-axis limit (:164-172); nothing rejects `index + count - 1 > limit`. `{axis:'column', index:18278, count:18278}` grows `colOrder` to ~36,556 entries while `MaxColumns` (:12) — the engine's grid bound also enforced for `clear` at :79 — is 18278. Cells pushed beyond column 18278 keep their ids in `colOrder` but sit at indices the grid cannot address, and formulas shifted onto them get 4-letter labels outside the documented range.

samples.summary: The delete endpoint echoes a negative `count` that does not match the request body
samples.evidence: `deleteAxis` parses `count` (always positive) and returns `this.applyShift(..., -count)`, whose response body is `{ axis, index, count }` with the negated value (controller :129, :201). A client that POSTs `{count: 1}` gets `{count: -1}` back; the engine's sign convention is an internal detail leaking into the public response.

samples.summary: Design doc still points at the pre-move frontend path for the relocated module
samples.evidence: `docs/design/sheets/comments.md:75` and `:289` reference `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-worksheet-structure.ts`, which this change renamed to `packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts`. Nested design docs are not covered by the backtick-path check, so nothing else will flag it.

verdict.reason: Code is present exactly as described and reachable in normal API use. `parseIndex`/`parseCount` (worksheet-structure.ts:118-156) bound only the coordinate by the axis extent (MaxRows=1e6, line 11) with no cap on the work implied; the same file caps clear-range area for precisely this reason (lines 14-30, 85-90). The validated values flow through worksheet-structure.controller.ts:112 -> applyShift (:174-205) into a synchronous `doc.update`, then applyWorksheetShift (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts:283-284) into insertWorksheetAxis (worksheet-axis.ts:25-45), which (a) pushes up to index-1 CRDT nodes one at a time via ensureAxisLength (:9-23), and (b) spreads up to 1e6 arguments into `order.splice` (:44) — above engine argument limits, a RangeError crash. createWorksheetAxisId (worksheet-record.ts:89-103) retries in an unbounded `for(;;)` against a 36^4 ≈ 1.68M ID space, and nothing caps total axis length, so repeated permitted inserts can make it never return. I found no other validator or clamp (grep: controller is the only caller of parseAxisShift/parseAxisMove), and the repo's own design doc (docs/design/sheets/axis-id-selection.md:192-206) names insertWorksheetAxis as an unbounded path that freezes at row 1,000,000. In-lane under Correctness as a crash/hang and broken invariant on a reachable path.

verdict.reason: The absence claim holds. The merge-split guard lives only in Sheet.moveCells (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1466-1471), which returns early when isMergeSplitByMove reports a partial overlap, before delegating to the store. The API endpoint moveAxis (packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-structure.controller.ts:133-168) calls applyWorksheetMove directly; applyWorksheetMove (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts:347-418) contains no such check and unconditionally does replaceMerges(ws, moveMergeMap(...)), and replaceMerges (:98-103) clears ws.merges first. parseAxisMove (packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-structure.ts:180-194) validates only axis/index/count/dst-inside-block and never inspects the worksheet, so it cannot enforce the invariant. I searched the whole backend for merge validation on this path and found none (only parseMerges for PUT /merges and the shape migration). One nuance: the concrete failure mode is usually corruption rather than deletion — moveMerge (merging.ts:103-137) remaps only the merge's start/end and takes min/max, so a half-moved merge is silently rewritten to span an expanded, wrong range (e.g. rows 3-5 with row 3 moved to row 10 becomes rows 4-9); the `if (!moved) continue;` drop at merging.ts:172 fires only for degenerate spans. Either way the state the UI is explicitly written to prevent is reachable via a normal POST .../move, so the finding is real and blocking under the correctness rubric (broken invariant / inconsistent persisted state on a reachable path).

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: applyWorksheetShift (worksheet-structure.ts:273-345) and applyWorksheetMove (:347-418) mutate axis order, formulas, dimensions, styles, rangeStyles, CF/DV, merges, anchors and threads, but never touch filter/hiddenRows/hiddenColumns/frozenRows/frozenCols, which are index-keyed persisted fields (worksheet-document.ts:85-98). worksheet-axis.ts (read in full) does not compensate either. The only place that compensation exists is the editor: sheet.ts:1317-1318 (shiftFilterState/shiftUserHiddenState), the freeze expand/shrink block at 1334-1359 and recomputeFilterHiddenRows() at 1363-1365 — reached via the frontend call site yorkie-store.ts:456,487. A repo-wide grep for shiftFilterState|shiftUserHiddenState|shiftHidden|shiftFreeze|shiftFrozen produces no hits under packages/backend, and the backend handlers (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:142-205) run only the two engine helpers plus the cross-tab range pass inside doc.update; the request-parsing helper packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-structure.ts does no state fixups. The affected state is real and API-visible: PUT freeze writes ws.frozenRows/frozenCols (worksheet.controller.ts:76-91) and PUT hidden writes ws.hiddenRows/hiddenColumns (:122-137), read back at :68-70 and :111-115. So after POST insert/delete/move the stored hidden indices, filter range and freeze boundary silently refer to shifted rows/columns — inconsistent index-keyed state on a normally reachable path, matching 'major' (wrong behavior/state left inconsistent, not a crash). No counterexample found in a wide search.

verdict.reason: Verified directly: rewriteFormulaCells (worksheet-structure.ts:85-95) spreads the existing cell and replaces only `f`, and the backend's normalizeCell (normalizeStoredCell, worksheet-grid.ts:241-243) explicitly preserves `v`, so the cached value survives a formula rewrite. The backend controller (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:147-154, 186-192) does nothing after applyWorksheetShift/Move, while the editor path recalculates at sheet.ts:1361 (helper at 1543-1549 calling calculate). ApiV1CellsController serves `cell?.v` verbatim (cells.controller.ts:63-72, 100-108). I searched wide for a counterexample — repo-wide greps for recalculate/recalc/calculateAll/buildDependants match only packages/sheets, packages/frontend and docs; `calc|evaluate|formula` under packages/backend/src matches only response-field names and prose comments; no headless engine instantiation in the backend; packages/cli has none either. The backend's own spec (worksheet-structure-axis.controller.spec.ts:78-92) asserts only the rewritten `f`, never a recalculated value. Blocking under the correctness rubric as major: after deleting a referenced row the document holds a rewritten formula next to its pre-delete value, and API readers get values inconsistent with the formulas until a client opens the doc.
